passage:
Last year I had two sealed rooms. In one was my education loan: three missed payments and a letter from the bank I kept in a drawer. In the other was my relationship, slowly ending over video calls. At work I was bright and efficient; nobody knew about either. With my boyfriend I never mentioned money. With my parents I never mentioned him. It worked, sort of. I kept functioning.
Then one Tuesday the bank called during a client meeting, and that same evening he said he wanted to break up. Both doors burst open at once. I sat in the office washroom and couldn't stop shaking. My friend Nazia found me there. I told her everything, the loan and the breakup, the first time I'd said both out loud. She didn't fix anything. She helped me write a list of who to call the next morning. I'm Shreya, and I keep fewer sealed rooms now.

qa.q: What did Shreya keep in a drawer?
qa.a: A letter from the bank.

qa.q: Why did keeping the two problems sealed apart work for Shreya, at least for a while?
qa.a: Separating them let Shreya stay bright and efficient at work and avoid facing both worries at once.

qa.q: What turning point helped Shreya begin to deal with both problems?
qa.a: Telling Nazia everything in the washroom and making a list of who to call the next morning, instead of sealing the doors again.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Nazia to find Shreya in the washroom?
qa.a: Probably alarming, since Shreya always seemed so capable, and moving to hear how much had been hidden.

grounding: An adult keeps a loan problem and a failing relationship in separate sealed compartments until both burst open on the same day.

passage:
Supervisor's note, 9 October
Sumit has been one of our steadiest engineers this year: calm in a crisis, never brings personal matters to work. Today that changed. During the client call he froze mid-sentence, excused himself, and I found him sitting in the stairwell with his head in his hands.
He told me, reluctantly, that his father's shop has been in debt for months and he has been sending money home, and that his marriage is strained because he hasn't told his wife. He said he kept work, money and home in "separate boxes" so he could keep functioning. This morning his wife found the bank messages and they argued; then the client call started.
Next steps: I gave him the rest of the day off. I pointed him to our confidential employee counselling line. We'll meet on Monday about his workload.
Urmila

qa.q: Where did Urmila find Sumit after the client call?
qa.a: Sitting in the stairwell with his head in his hands.

qa.q: Why did keeping work, money and home in 'separate boxes' feel necessary to Sumit?
qa.a: Sumit felt overwhelmed by the debt and the strain at home, and the boxes let him keep functioning at work without facing everything at once.

qa.q: Which of Urmila's steps is most useful, and why?
qa.a: Pointing him to the confidential counselling line, because he needs somewhere to open the boxes with support, not just a day off.

qa.q: How might Sumit's wife have felt finding the bank messages?
qa.a: Shocked and hurt at being shut out of something so big, which is why they argued.

grounding: A supervisor records how an engineer who kept money worries out of his marriage and home worries out of work cracked when both pressed at once.

passage:
Sunday night
Tried to count today how many things I don't say to whom. At work: nothing about Damini and me arguing every night about whether to move to Pune. With Damini: nothing about the credit-card balance I've been rolling over since Diwali. With Ammi: nothing about either. I've built a flat with every door locked. It means I can go to work and be "good old Tanvir", and come home and be... quiet.
Tonight Damini asked why I flinch when my phone buzzes. I almost told her. Instead I said, "Work stuff." The lie sat in my stomach all evening.
I can feel the walls creaking. One day the bank and the Pune decision will land in the same week, and I'll crack.
Tomorrow I'll tell Damini about the card. Just one door. One at a time.
Tanvir

qa.q: What did Tanvir tell Damini when she asked about the flinching?
qa.a: "Work stuff."

qa.q: Why does keeping every door locked feel useful to Tanvir?
qa.a: Tanvir dreads the painful conversations, and locking every door lets Tanvir function at work without facing them, even though the lie leaves Tanvir uneasy all evening.

qa.q: What choice does Tanvir make for tomorrow, and why is it a good first step?
qa.a: Telling Damini about the card, opening one door at a time before the pressures arrive together.

qa.q: How might Damini feel noticing the flinch at every phone buzz?
qa.a: Worried and perhaps shut out, sensing something is being hidden but not knowing what.

grounding: An adult keeps a credit-card problem out of a relationship and relationship trouble out of work, feels the walls creaking, and decides to open one door.

passage:
Noor: are you free? i'm in the office bathroom
Thomas: what happened?
Noor: two things at once. the bank called about the card during the client review. third call this month
Noor: and while i was declining it, Sam texted "we need to talk tonight"
Noor: i've kept these apart for months. work doesn't know about the money, Sam doesn't know about the money, nobody at work knows about Sam
Noor: today they all hit at the same time and i walked out mid-presentation
Thomas: ok. breathe. you're not in trouble with me
Thomas: those walls kept you going. but that's a lot to carry alone
Noor: i know
Thomas: can you tell your manager you need twenty minutes? then tonight, one thing at a time
Thomas: and for the card, maybe book a session with a proper debt counsellor this week. i'll sit with you when you call
Noor: ok. yes. thank you

qa.q: What did Sam text during the client review?
qa.a: "We need to talk tonight."

qa.q: Why did Noor walk out mid-presentation?
qa.a: The worries Noor had kept sealed apart, the money and Sam, pressed in at the same moment, and the walls that usually made work possible gave way.

qa.q: What steps does Thomas suggest to get through this?
qa.a: Asking the manager for twenty minutes, handling one thing at a time tonight, and booking a debt counsellor this week with Thomas there for the call.

qa.q: How might Noor's colleagues have seen the walk-out?
qa.a: Knowing nothing about the money or Sam, colleagues would likely be puzzled or worried, since Noor usually seems to have everything under control.

grounding: Shows an adult who has kept a money problem and a relationship problem walled off from each other and from work, until both press at once and the walls crack.

passage:
Jaya ran the small grocery shop at the Bundi bus stand like clockwork: accounts neat, customers greeted by name, jokes for the schoolchildren buying toffees. Nobody would have guessed at the two locked rooms she carried.
In one: the wholesaler's bill, three months unpaid, which she had never mentioned to anyone. In the other: Gautam, her husband, who wanted to move to Jaipur for work, and the quiet fights they'd been having every night. She never spoke of Gautam at the shop, or of the bill at home.
On Thursday both doors opened at once. The wholesaler's man arrived asking loudly for payment, just as Gautam walked in to argue about Jaipur. Customers turned. Jaya's hands shook so badly she dropped a jar of pickle on the floor.
That night she told Gautam everything about the bill. He was silent for a long time. Then he said, "Tomorrow we go to the cooperative bank together and ask for proper advice. After that, we talk about Jaipur."

qa.q: What did Jaya drop when both problems arrived at once?
qa.a: A jar of pickle.

qa.q: Why had keeping the bill and the fights in separate rooms felt useful to Jaya?
qa.a: It let her run the shop smoothly and stay cheerful with customers, instead of being swamped by both worries at once.

qa.q: What turning point came after the walls cracked?
qa.a: Telling Gautam everything about the bill that night, which led to a plan to go to the cooperative bank together for proper advice and then talk about Jaipur.

qa.q: How might Gautam have felt learning about the three-month-old bill?
qa.a: Gautam was probably shocked and hurt at being kept out, but his calm plan for the next day shows he wanted to face it together.

grounding: Illustrates an adult who keeps a debt away from her marriage and her marriage away from her shop, until both burst in at once and she chooses to share them.
